title: Dynamic Eviction Grace Periods and Burst Prioritization for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Asha Patel
description: PRD for introducing an adaptive eviction grace period and burst prioritization mechanism for Dedicated capacity. This feature aims to reduce customer-visible disruptions during transient overloads by extending soft-eviction grace dynamically and prioritizing short bursts for tenants with burst credits while preserving SLOs for reserved workloads.
background: Customers on Dedicated capacity have asked for fewer interruptions during short, high-traffic spikes without undermining isolation guarantees for reserved pools. Current fixed eviction windows are too aggressive for workloads with spiky tail behavior, causing failed requests and degraded UX. Conversely, overly permissive policies increase noisy-neighbor risk. We need a middle ground that adapts to workload patterns and tenant entitlements.
goals: Reduce failed or preempted requests caused by short transient spikes by at least 40% for eligible tenants
Provide deterministic, auditable rules that preserve reserved SLOs while allowing controlled soft bursts
Expose controls and observability in Console for burst credit consumption and eviction behavior
Allow safe rollbacks and gradual rollout with feature flags per org/zone
success_metrics: P99 request failure rate during spikes for tenants with burst credits reduced by >=40% compared to baseline
No more than 2% increase in tail latency for reserved-class requests during bursts
Console shows burst-credit balance and last-eviction timestamp for 100% of affected tenants
<1% incidents attributed to burst-prioritization logic in first 8 weeks post-rollout
non_goals: Overhaul of global autoscaler logic (this PRD augments eviction/prioritization only)
Introducing hard capacity overcommit beyond current safety thresholds
Changing pricing or billing model tied to burst credits in this rollout
scope_included: Eviction controller: add adaptive grace window algorithm and config knobs
Burst credit ledger: per-tenant short-burst credit accounting (time-decayed)
Routing policy: prefer non-preemptive paths for active burst-credit tenants when safe
Console: UI surfaces for burst-credit balance, grace-window overrides, and per-tenant recent evictions
APIs: admin endpoints to query and set burst policy per org/zone
Telemetry: new metrics (burst_credit_used, eviction_grace_ms, preempted_requests, credit_refill_rate)
scope_excluded: Rewriting request prioritization across multi-tenant shared clusters
Private deployment packaging changes beyond config flags
user_stories: As an SRE for an enterprise tenant, I want short spikes to be allowed without immediate preemption so my product can absorb transient user demand
As a Platform Engineer, I want visibility into which tenants consumed burst credits and when so I can investigate performance regressions
As a Product Manager, I want to define organization-level burst policies and safe upper bounds so we can trade cost vs availability
As an Operator, I want automatic decay and refill rules for credits so credits don't accumulate indefinitely
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive grace window exists and can be configured by policy with at least three parameters: base_ms, scale_factor, max_ms
System honors burst credits: when tenant has credit > 0 and grace window active, requests are not preempted unless reserved SLO would be violated
Automated integration test simulating 1000s TPS spike shows >=40% fewer preemptions for a tenant with credits vs no-credits baseline
Console surfaces: (1) burst credit current balance, (2) last grace-window duration, and (3) recent preemption events for the tenant
New metrics (burst_credit_used, eviction_grace_ms) emitted to telemetry and visible in dashboards with retention 30 days
Feature flag gate present and rollback procedure documented: toggling flag immediately disables credit consumption and reverts to fixed eviction behavior
Security review completed and audit log entries recorded for policy changes
Documentation: PRD linked guides for operators, API reference for admins, and runbook for oncall
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal dogfood in staging with synthetic spike tests (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Roll to 10% of production orgs (non-critical) behind feature flag, monitor key metrics (2 weeks)
Phase 3: Increase to 50% with automatic safety rollback triggers (2 weeks)
Phase 4: Full rollout after 6 weeks of stable signals and support readiness
Always-on: Gradual ramp with canary policies by region and capacity class
dependencies: DES-1204: Console UI mockups and component implementation
SEC-331: audit-log retention for policy changes
risks: Incorrect tuning could weaken reserved SLOs — mitigated by conservative defaults and hard caps
Burst credits could be gamed by tenants — mitigated by decay rules and per-org limits
Telemetry gaps could make debugging hard — engineers must add end-to-end tests and dashboards
Rollout might interact poorly with existing autoscaler leading to oscillation — require hysteresis and rate limits
engineering_notes: Algorithm sketch: compute grace_ms = min(max_ms, base_ms * (1 + scale_factor * recent_spike_zscore))
Credit model: integer credit tokens consumed per request category (small/med/large) with time-based refill (tokens/hour)
Backstop: global hard eviction threshold that cannot be bypassed by credits to protect reserved pools
Testing: create load harness that replays traffic traces from 3 tenants with different spike profiles
Observability: add burn-rate alerts when credit consumption exceeds expected baseline by 2x
